newsitem.title: USA: Great Western doubts Ahmanson layoff claim.
newsitem.headline: Great Western doubts Ahmanson layoff claim.

text.p: A promise from H.F. Ahmanson and Co that any layoffs in a merger with Great Western Financial Corp will be kept to a minimum was greeted with skepticism by a source close to Great Western Monday.

The source noted that Ahmanson has stated in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) that it anticipates incurring $325 million of merger costs relating to Great Western's "premises, severance and operations."

"A big part of branch consolidation is people," the source said, adding that statements made by Ahmanson chairman and chief executive Charles Rinehart and other material originating with Ahmanson have been "inconsistent." Rinehart on Friday sent a letter to Great Western directors saying layoffs at Great Western could be kept to a minimum. He also said decisions about Ahmanson and Great Western employees in similar positions would be made on the merits.

The source also questioned why Ahmanson seemed to be taking pot shots at the economics of joining Great Western with various friendly suitors such as Washington Mutual Savings Bank when no formal bids have announced.

Washington Mutual earlier Monday said it would not comment on rumors or speuclation but added that it was interested in growth in California both internally and via acquisitions. Ahmanson announced its bid for Great Western February 18. Although Great Western has not formally responded, the Ahmanson bid, worth about $6 billion, is widely viewed on Wall Street as a hostile takeover attempt.
